parts.problem_md:
Fig. 9.1 shows the arrangements of particles in ethanol and sulfur at a temperature of 25 °C.

![Two square containers labelled X and Y: X is tightly packed with equal circles in a grid, Y has the same circles loosely packed with gaps between them](assets/001-two-square-containers-labelled-x-and-y-x-is-tigh.png)

**Fig. 9.1**

Use Fig. 9.1 and information from Table 9.1 to state which diagram, X or Y, shows the structure of ethanol and of sulfur at 25°C.

Explain your answer in terms of particles.

ethanol: ..................

sulfur: ..................

explanation: ..................
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - ethanol: Y AND sulfur: X AND at 25 °C, sulfur is solid and ethanol is liquid **[1 mark]**
> - solid has a regular particle arrangement / liquid has an irregular particle arrangement / solid has more closely packed particles / liquid has less closely packed particles **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Link the particle diagram to the state of matter first (regular, close-packed particles = solid; irregular, more spread out particles = liquid), then use that to match each substance to its correct diagram.

parts.problem_md:
A sample of a substance has a definite shape and a definite volume.

The substance changes state. The sample now has **no** definite shape but still has a definite volume.

What is the name of the change of state?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is D**

- A solid has a definite shape and a definite volume
- A liquid has no definite shape but still has a definite volume
- The change from solid to liquid is melting
